transcript.text: I think my washer dryer has a fault - I put it on just a drying programme with dry-ish clothes and I can hear water running into it and draining the whole time. Surely it shouldn't use water to dry? It's a Beko.

It is actually normal for many Beko washer-dryers to fill with water during a drying cycle, as they use cold water to condense the moisture from your clothes rather than using a heating element like a tumble dryer. The draining you hear is simply the machine pumping that condensed water away through the filter and hose. Since this sounds like standard operation, I would suggest checking if the drum feels warm to the touch; if it is getting hot but staying damp, we should look at airflow or load size, whereas if it stays cold, the heating element may not be engaging.

I haven't felt the drum while it's running, so I can't say whether it's warm. The clothes do come out properly dry at the end, though, and there are no error codes. So is the water use really normal, and not a fault?

Yes, it is completely normal for Beko washer-dryers to fill and drain water during a drying programme because they use cold water to condense moisture from your clothes rather than just blowing hot air. Since your clothes are coming out properly dry and there are no error codes, this suggests the machine is functioning as intended. The most common reason people worry about this is not realising that the "drying" phase involves significant water usage for condensation. You don't need to do any checks right now as the appliance appears to be working correctly.
